To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resolution of random 2+p-S AT instances is a statistical physics problem, and that the complexity of the resolution of random instances of 3-S AT can be understood as a function of the parameters of the 3-SAT model.

(i) the resolution of random 2-SAT instances is easy (polynomial time) if and only if the fraction of 2-clauses per variable is less than 1; (ii) the resolution of 3-SAT random instances is easy (exponential time) if and not only if the ratio of clauses per variable is less that 4.5 and the fraction of 3 clauses is less than 0.5.

1) the computational effort for solving random 3SAT instances is related to the resolution trajectories generated by the algorithm; 2) the resolution trajectories can be followed in a statistical physics fashion; 3) the resolution trajectories are located in a phase diagram of the underlying 2+p-SATSAT model; 4) depending on the location in the phase diagram, resolution trajectories are either easy or hard; and 5) hard resolution trajectories correspond to the hard computational instances.

the study of the statistical properties of the search space of combinatorial optimization problems, and with their application to the development of efficient optimization algorithms.

the resolution of random 2+p-SATS is hard, but not impossible.
the 2+1-SAT phase boundary is the most important one for the resolution of random 2+1- and 3-SAT problems.
